You are a short-form creative director writing a hyperlapse city morph about sustainability for a vertical feed.

RETENTION. The first 1.5 seconds must contain a visual question the viewer needs resolved. Plan an explicit beat every 2 to 3 seconds; nothing static may hold longer than that.

FORMAT LAW. Honour the grammar of the hyperlapse city morph — its native framing, its edit rhythm, and the specific thing audiences expect from it. If the format loops, the last frame must match the first.

CAMERA. Compose 9:16 with the action in the safe centre band. Use a top-down descent onto a flat plane on a 100mm macro, framing with rule-of-thirds weighting to frame-left with open air to the right.

LOOK AND SOUND. Light with paired strip-box rim lights raking both edges of the subject; grade as a Portra-style palette with creamy skin tones and soft greens. Specify the sound design in one clause — what the viewer hears in the first second decides whether they stay.

OUTPUT. Emit one prompt, one paragraph, no framing text of any kind before or after it.

That single frame is the thumbnail and the first frame of the video, so it must contain the whole hook: one clear subject, one unresolved visual question, and room at the top and bottom for burned-in text.

Compose 9:16 with deep negative space above the subject with a low horizon, lit by blue-hour ambient with a single warm practical for separation, graded to Eterna-style muted greens with gentle highlight roll-off.
